hard_feasibility.policy: All hard constraints must PASS for a candidate to be feasible. Soft thresholds may FAIL without infeasibility but incur distributional penalty via soft objectives. Hard is write-once gate; soft is Pareto objective.
hard_feasibility.evaluation: Feasibility first, then Pareto ranking of soft distributional deviations. Rejection on any hard FAIL regardless of soft scores.
hard_feasibility.note_hard_vs_soft: C018 demonstrates the split: P(CV_E>0.5)=0.207-0.248 (seed0/seed1) and max CV_E=1.98/2.27 PASS hard (thresholds >=0.15 and >=1.5), while mean CV_ISI=0.344/0.373 FAILS soft B2 mean [0.5,1.5] — C018 is HARD-FEASIBLE despite soft mean FAIL. This is intentional: hard protects typed E diversity P(CV_E) not collapsing to Gen-1 unimodal regular, not scalar mean. Mean CV alone is soft distributional, not hard feasibility.

soft_objectives_distributional.policy: Soft objectives are DISTRIBUTIONS not scalar |bar_r - 7.5|. Each J_k is a distance between observed distribution P_observed and broad provenance-backed neighborhood P_target (uniform or Gaussian blob). Optimizing any single mean alone is insufficient and prohibited as sole progress criterion (see c011_counterexample). Require Pareto dominance or constrained improvement (all J_k not worsened beyond tolerance, at least one improved).

c011_counterexample.claim: Optimizing means alone insufficient: C011 tonic scale 0.7 moved bar_r toward speculative mean ~6.6 while rho worsened 0.354->0.44, demonstrating scalar mean improvement can co-degrade synchrony.
c011_counterexample.evidence: C011 tonic 5.0->3.5 gave r_E 10.59->3.89 and bar_r ~6.6 near B1 global 3-15, but rho 0.354->0.44 and Var collapse noted in review_CL1_AGSDR_readiness §3; lineage C012-C017 similarly Var->CV chain falsified. Hence scalar J=|bar_r-7.5| would call progress while B2 rho and CV flat/falsified.
c011_counterexample.implication: AGSDR must be Pareto/constraint-based, not single-scalar minimization. Scalarized weighted sum J=Sigma w_k J_k with w=1/6 is only a baseline tie-breaker among Pareto-nondominated feasible candidates, never a replacement for feasibility gate.

optimization_policy.not: simple scalar sum J=Sigma w_k J_k as primary progress criterion
optimization_policy.reason: Mean-only scalarization hides tradeoffs (C011). Feasibility (hard) must dominate; scalarization only ranks among Pareto-nondominated feasible candidates.

algorithm_spec.feasibility_first: All candidates evaluated against hard constraints table (H01-H12). Any hard FAIL => infeasible, rejected, no scalar comparison.
algorithm_spec.pareto_ranking: Among feasible, compute soft distributional distances J = (J_rates,J_irregularity,J_synchrony,J_Fano,J_hetero,J_EI,J_CL1C). Candidate A dominates B if for all k J_k(A) <= J_k(B) with strict < for at least one k, without worsening any beyond tolerance epsilon=0.05. Nondominated set kept.
algorithm_spec.scalar_baseline_tiebreaker: Within nondominated front, rank by scalarized J_scalar = Sigma w_k * normalized_J_k with w_k=1/6 frozen equal (B10). This defines w=1/6 baseline with Pareto ranking as tasked. Normalized J_k each [0,1] where 0 is within target neighborhood, 1 is hard FAIL boundary. w frozen, no empirical T1-T7 weighting.
